newsitem.title: USA: Ore. vote on Enron, Portland deal set Jun 4.
newsitem.headline: Ore. vote on Enron, Portland deal set Jun 4.

text.p: The Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC) will make a final decision on the planned merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co on June 4, under a revised review schedule, a spokeswoman for the Portland utility said Friday.
The commission was expected to vote on the deal March 17, but failed negotiations over a rate cut for Oregon electricity customers led to the schedule revision.
Under the new schedule, staff of the commission will issue a final report and proposed order on April 11, with comments due on April 29.
Oral arguments will be presented to the OPUC on May 6 and a final order will be issued June 4, the spokeswoman said.
In addition, a pre-hearing conference on merger terms will be held April 16, during which the sides will determine if there is a need to hold a "contested case hearing."
If such a hearing is held, the review schedule would need to be changed again, the Portland General spokeswoman said.
The companies met Wednesday with the commission staff in Salem, Ore., to work out the rate cut issue, but failed to reach agreement.
Enron's standing offer is for a rate cut of $61 million, including $9 million per year for four years in cost of service reductions.
The commission staff, however, is holding out for a cut of $141 million, including the same $9 million for four years in cost savings.
